Job Summary: In this role, you will provide technical leadership, coaching, and oversight to project ESH teams across a portfolio of manufacturing and technology projects. You will help strengthen ESH management systems, improve program consistency, support risk-based execution, and partner with project leadership to address significant concerns.

This role offers the opportunity to influence ESH performance at both the project and portfolio level while supporting high-impact work in fast-paced environments. #LI-AE2 Major Responsibilities: Shape strong project starts by providing ESH input to proposals, execution planning, risk assessments, resourcing strategies, and readiness activities.

Strengthen project ESH performance by coaching teams on ESH management plans, execution plans, permit-to-work systems, contractor management, and related specialty programs.

Drive consistent, high-quality ESH execution by overseeing program implementation and continuous improvement in alignment with applicable regulations and recognized management system requirements.

Improve program effectiveness by leading assessments, readiness reviews, audits, and conformance checks, and by helping teams close findings in a timely manner. Embed ESH into project delivery by partnering with engineering, construction, supply chain, subcontracts, commissioning, and project controls teams.

Advance portfolio learning and consistency by facilitating program kickoffs, risk workshops, constructability reviews, management system reviews, and knowledge-sharing forums. Support informed decision-making by preparing and reviewing ESH documentation, compliance reports, risk registers, objectives, and regulatory submittals.

Build alignment across stakeholders by working with project leadership, customers, regulators, auditors, and internal partners to address issues and coordinate support. Enhance visibility and execution performance by supporting ESH digitization initiatives and practical tools and systems.

Intervene on critical ESH concerns, including recommending or exercising stop-work authority, when conditions present unacceptable risk to people, the environment, or communities.

Master's degree in a related field with 12+ years of experience advancing ESH performance in complex project settings. At least 5 years of experience supporting semiconductor, pharmaceutical/biotech, or hyperscale data center projects, with demonstrated impact on ESH performance.

Experience leading or advising ESH performance across multiple projects and influencing teams in a matrixed or functional environment. Strong knowledge of ESH regulations, industry standards, and management systems, including ISO 14001 and ISO 45001, with the ability to apply requirements in project execution.

Experience strengthening risk-based ESH programs through incident investigation, corrective action management, and continuous improvement. Ability to manage competing priorities, communicate effectively with diverse stakeholders, and support teams in fast-paced project environments.

Familiarity with contractor management, compliance reviews, and contract requirements that support strong ESH outcomes. Valid driver's license required. Required Knowledge and Skills: Professional certification such as ASP, OHST, CSP, or CIH.

Working knowledge of OSHA, EPA, and key environmental regulations, with the ability to support practical compliance. Knowledge of industrial hygiene principles and chemical hazard management.

Field Operations Manager Location Remote (U.S.) with occasional travel to customer sites, TurbineOne facilities, demonstrations, and operational events as required. About TurbineOne TurbineOne is building Mission-AI for the Frontlines.

Our Frontline Perception System (FPS) helps military and national security operators detect threats, accelerate decision-making, and unlock the power of AI at the tactical edge. We endeavor to build mission-valuable products in command and control, autonomy, and AI-enabled mission systems.

We partner directly with frontline users to deliver mission-ready capabilities that work in real-world environments where speed, trust, reliability, and operational resilience matter most. Our team is composed of experienced technologists, veterans, and operators committed to advancing national security through responsible innovation.

The Role The Field Operations Manager owns the operational systems that make Field Engineering deployable, repeatable, and scalable. This is a builder role; you will start as an Individual Contributor (IC) with extended team support, responsible for defining the operational models and discipline.

Over time, you will build and lead a team to perform these functions. You will partner closely with Field Engineering, Mission Operations, Product, Engineering, Security, BD, and leadership to ensure every field engagement has the right people, equipment, information, and operating cadence to succeed. Core Responsibility Areas

Field Engagement Operations: Own the end-to-end operational workflow for Field Engineering from resourcing and readiness to execution and closeout. Maintain the field engagement tracker, validate upcoming requests, and drive pre-deployment planning discipline.

Field Hardware: Own the operational readiness of field hardware. Coordinate imaging, configuration, software versioning, testing, and shipping for deployments and demos. Maintain standard loadouts and coordinate with Engineering/IT/DevOps.

Field Asset Management: Create and maintain the asset-management system. Track inventory, custody, location, status, and lifecycle management for all field gear.

Field Knowledge Management: Own the field knowledge base. Maintain SOPs, checklists, templates, and AARs. Ensure lessons learned are captured and reusable.

Field Communications: Own communication rhythms. Translate product updates into field-relevant guidance, coordinate daily SITREPs, and provide operational updates to leadership.

Field Enablement: Own the Field Engineering readiness model. Build onboarding pathways, define readiness requirements, and run enablement sessions and assessments to ensure FEs are prepared for mission types and hardware loadouts.

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, or a related technical discipline, or equivalent practical experience.
4+ years of experience in Field Operations, Technical Enablement, Customer Success, or Systems Engineering, with a specific focus on building and scaling operational systems.
2+ years of experience leading or managing teams (this role transitions from a hands-on IC builder to a team lead).
Proven track record of operationalizing informal or ad-hoc processes into repeatable, scalable operating models.

The Field Engineering team consistently executes against clearly defined priorities with high reliability across all customer sites.
Customer deployments occur smoothly with minimal operational disruption.
Field Engineering tools and processes mature over time to support the growth of the company.

Field Engineering is viewed as a strategic enabler that bridges the gap between core engineering and tactical mission success.

You'll join a team of experienced technologists, veterans, and mission-focused professionals committed to solving some of the nation's most challenging operational problems through responsible innovation.

About Maneva Maneva is an AI services company founded by a former Google DeepMind researcher, focused on transforming manufacturing operations through advanced AI. We enable autonomous factory operation and optimization by generating AI-driven actions and insights using off-the-shelf hardware or existing vision systems.

Role Overview Maneva is seeking a People & Business Operations Manager to build and lead our people operations function at a critical stage of growth.

This role sits at the intersection of employee lifecycle management, governance, business operations, and culture.

You'll own performance management infrastructure, compensation and benefits administration, employee relations, U.S. state-level employment compliance as we expand our U.S. footprint, and will help drive the initiatives of the strategy and business operations team.

You'll be responsible for building the systems that let us hire, develop, and retain great people as we continue our fast expansion. You'll work closely with the Talent Manager, Finance, Business Operations, and the broader executive leadership team, and act as a trusted advisor to the CEO and leadership team on people matters.

Key Responsibilities U.S. Employment Compliance Own state-by-state compliance as Maneva expands its U.S. employee base: tax registration, payroll setup, mandatory workplace posters, and required employee notices, all of which vary by state.

Build and maintain a repeatable process for evaluating new-state requirements as hiring expands, rather than handling each state reactively. Partner with Rippling, outside counsel, and Finance to ensure payroll, tax, and notice obligations are met on schedule for every state in which Maneva has employees.

Serve as Maneva 's go-to internal expert on U.S. state employment law as it applies to a distributed, remote-first workforce. Performance Management & Levelling Design and execute performance review cycles (6-month and annual) across the organization, tailored to company growth stage and business needs.

Own and maintain levelling frameworks across engineering (IC1–IC6) and non-technical roles; define competencies, expectations, and progression criteria, building on the framework already in place. Partner with department heads and the Talent Manager to calibrate performance data and inform talent decisions.

Design and facilitate manager training on feedback, goal-setting, and performance conversations. Maintain performance documentation and analytics to inform strategic people decisions. Compensation Administration Own day-to-day execution of compensation administration across all job levels and geographies; maintain salary bands.

Execute variable/commission plans for sales and other roles; ensure alignment with business goals. Execute ROE submissions, payroll adjustments, and comp/commission payouts, routing every payout through Finance for cost sign-off. Handle market increases, retention bonuses, and compensation requests with appropriate approvals.

Benefits & Wellness Administration Own benefits administration across the US and Canada. Coordinate benefits enrollment, education, and communication; manage plan changes. Administer COBRA coverage, health plan compliance, and employee welfare programs. Track and optimize benefits costs; provide leadership with regular reporting.

Contracts, Policies & Compliance Maintain and update U.S. and Canadian employment agreement templates. Own employee handbook and policy management for both Canada and the U.S.; refresh as laws and entities change. Manage people-related compliance: ROE submissions, payroll tax filings, and employment law compliance across all jurisdictions.

Maintain data integrity across HRIS systems; ensure clean records for auditing. Coordinate with external employment counsel as needed. Culture & Employee Engagement Partner with the Talent Manager on culture initiatives and engagement programs. Own recognition programs, including birthday and work-anniversary recognition.

Monitor and report on employee engagement signals; identify retention risks. Facilitate communication between leadership and employees. Systems, Automation & Operations Build automated workflows. Create dashboards and reporting for leadership on key HR metrics. Manage systems integration; ensure clean data flow between platforms.

Take ownership of ad-hoc projects and strategic initiatives. Business Operations Support Provide flexible support on cross-functional business initiatives as they arise — this portion of the role is intentionally variable rather than a fixed list of duties. Assist with insurance requirements and vendor/partnership coordination as needed.

Support with ad-hoc strategic initiatives such as fundraising and data room management, and partnership outreach. Support KPI and revenue schedule tracking in coordination with Finance Expect this allocation to flex up (e.g., during fundraising) and back down as business needs shift.

Requirements Required Experience 5+ years in people operations or HR, with experience scaling a company from roughly 50–300+ employees. Hands-on, current experience with U.S. state-level employment compliance — tax registration, payroll considerations, mandatory workplace posters, and employee notices — required.

Success leading people ops teams or managing complex, multi-jurisdiction workflows. Hands-on HRIS experience with Rippling; benefits administration. Track record designing performance cycles, levelling frameworks, and compensation structures. Based in Canada, ideally the Greater Toronto Area.

Core Competencies Deep, current knowledge of U.S. state employment law and how it varies by jurisdiction. Systems thinking and process design; ability to build scalable workflows. Strong stakeholder management across Finance, IT, Recruitment, and Leadership. Data-driven mindset; ability to turn HR data into clear recommendations.

Calm under pressure; ability to manage ambiguity, shifting priorities, and organizational change — including flexing between People Ops and BizOps work as needed. Attention to detail and compliance rigor. Clear communication; ability to explain HR and compliance concepts to non-experts.

Passion for building cultures where people feel valued and connected to mission. Technical Skills & Tools Proficiency with HRIS systems (Rippling preferred). Comfort building automation tools. Strong Excel and analytics skills. Nice to Have Experience in B2B SaaS, deep tech, or AI/manufacturing.

Familiarity with venture-backed, fast-growth company dynamics, including fundraise support. French language skills. Why Join Maneva Build an expanded people operations function from the ground up at a mission-driven AI company in a period of fast growth across Canada and the U.S.

You'll own the full employee lifecycle, lead Maneva 's U.S. compliance posture, and have direct influence on culture, talent strategy, and organizational effectiveness. Work closely with a collaborative leadership team.

You'll have autonomy to design systems, make strategic recommendations, and directly impact how Maneva attracts, develops, and retains world-class people — with occasional exposure to fundraising and broader business operations.

About Substrate
Substrate is the critical infrastructure layer between AI and biology. AI for biology has a data problem, not a compute problem: biological foundation models can predict but cannot experiment, and the large-scale, high-quality data they need does not exist. We are building the lab that generates it, with quality and provenance built in. We are not a CRO and we are not a cloud lab.
The company was founded by Mostafa ElSayed, co-founder and CEO; Oli Hoy, who leads the lab buildout and operations; Alexey Morgunov, who leads science and intelligence software; and Anna Huyghues-Despointes, who leads partnerships and go-to-market.

You will run the day-to-day operations of our lab in London, and be the person the scientists come to when something is missing, broken, late or lost. The day-one work is what you would expect: consumables and stock, goods in and cold chain, equipment servicing and calibration, suppliers and purchasing, waste streams and safety records.
Three parts go beyond a standard lab operations job. The first is provenance. Every experiment we sell carries a record of what went into it, down to the lot of the consumable used and the conditions material was held in. If a lot number is not captured, the data point is worth less, and that record runs through you.
The second is that the systems are not written yet. Inventory, goods in, asset registers and ordering exist in no form that will survive the next year. You define what the lab has to capture and work with the science and software teams to make sure it does.
The third is that sample handling and stock control here get automated, and you help specify the system that does it. Every sample, plate, reagent and consumable lot carries a barcode, scanned at each point it is handled, so the record is created by the work rather than reconstructed afterwards.

The same scan draws stock down, which turns reordering from a weekly count into something the system flags before anyone is short. Our software team is building that layer now and the requirements have to come from the lab floor: what gets a barcode, where the scan points sit, and what happens when a label will not read.

Some find that energising; some find it outside their lane. Worth knowing which one you are.
Your first 90 days
First 30 days
Take ownership of goods in: every delivery received, booked in, stored correctly and recorded.
Map how material moves through the lab and build the first accurate picture of what we hold. That map is the input to a fully barcoded scheme and system.
Days 30 to 60
Put a working inventory and reorder system in place, with minimum levels set from real consumption rather than guesses, and own the purchasing loop.
Agree the barcode and labelling scheme with the software team, and get equipment records in one place.
Days 60 to 90
Run the lab as a routine that does not depend on being asked, with the barcoded system live across one workflow, goods-in to bench to stock draw-down, feeding our provenance record.

You have run the physical side of a lab where being out of stock stops the work: biotech, pharma, a university or institute lab, or a manufacturing or diagnostics operation built around one.

Lab consumables and the rhythm of a working lab are already familiar to you, you have handled real volume and real inventory, and you know the difference between a system that works on paper and one that works at eight on a Monday morning.

We are not asking for a particular speciality, but you should arrive able to run the lab rather than learn what one needs.

Two or more years running a lab or comparable physical operation, hands-on and accountable for the result.
Practical stock control: goods in, inventory records, reorder points, stock counts that reconcile.
Buying from suppliers: raising orders, comparing quotes, managing lead times.
Hands-on with a barcoded or scanned stock system, including what goes wrong when people skip the scan.
Lab environment experience: cold storage, hazardous waste, containment, controlled materials.

How we work and who you will work with
This role is on site five days a week at 20 Triton Street in London, because the lab is a physical place and the work is in it. The wider founding team is distributed across London, New York and Europe.

You will report to Simon Varzandeh, a member of our scientific staff working on protein characterisation and one of the lab's heaviest users, and work alongside the protein science and functional genomics teams, the engineers building the tracking and stock system with you, and operations on facilities, health and safety and purchasing.

You will be the first person here whose whole job is focused on the lab floor.
